vocab_words.meaning: Having an obstinately uncooperative attitude toward authority or discipline.
vocab_words.example_sentence: The international community urged recalcitrant non-state actors to abide by global safety protocols.

vocab_words.meaning: Nearness in place, time, or relationship.
vocab_words.example_sentence: The geographical propinquity of the two neighboring nations mandates strong bilateral economic ties.

vocab_words.meaning: To remove or prevent a difficulty, problem, or need.
vocab_words.example_sentence: The expansion of the Dedicated Freight Corridor will obviate logistics delays for heavy cargo.

vocab_words.meaning: Able to be maintained or defended against attack or objection.
vocab_words.example_sentence: Without empirical data on social benefits, maintaining direct cash doles becomes economically untenable.
Engaging in puerile political spats during international summits undermines diplomatic decorum.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: To gain an advantage over someone secretly or unexpectedly.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: By heavily investing in deep-tech startups, India hopes to steal a march on global competitors in emerging fields.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: To work or study late into the night.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: Diplomats burned the midnight oil to finalize the joint declaration before the summit concluded.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: Likely to happen or appear in the near future.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: A comprehensive overhaul of national economic base-year data is reported to be in the offing.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: A minor drawback or difficulty that spoils something that would otherwise be pleasant or successful.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: The lack of unified digital payment infrastructure proved to be the main fly in the ointment during cross-border transactions.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: Undecided or neutral regarding a particular issue.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: Several member nations remained on the fence regarding the creation of a unified trade currency.

static_gk_boosters.title: Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India (DFCCIL)
bullets: Established in October 2006 under the Companies Act 1956 as a Special Purpose Vehicle owned by the Ministry of Railways.
Responsible for planning, construction, maintenance, and operation of two major corridors: Eastern DFC (Ludhiana to Dankuni) and Western DFC (Dadri to JNPT).
Headquartered in New Delhi.

static_gk_boosters.title: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR)
bullets: Statutory body constituted in March 2007 under the Commission for Protection of Child Rights (CPCR) Act, 2005.
Operates under the administrative control of the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
Ensures all laws, policies, and administrative mechanisms align with child rights perspectives as per the Indian Constitution and UN Convention on the Rights of the Child.

static_gk_boosters.title: BRICS & New Development Bank (NDB)
bullets: BRIC term was coined in 2001 by Jim O'Neill; first formal summit held in Yekaterinburg, Russia in 2009.
New Development Bank (NDB) was set up during the 6th BRICS Summit in Fortaleza (2014) with equal voting rights among founding members.
NDB is headquartered in Shanghai, China.

static_gk_boosters.title: National Statistical Office (NSO)
bullets: Formed by merging the Central Statistics Office (CSO) and National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) under MoSPI.
Responsible for publishing key national indicators including Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Index of Industrial Production (IIP), and Consumer Price Index (CPI).
Current base year for GDP calculation in India is 2011-12.

static_gk_boosters.title: Asian Cricket Council (ACC)
bullets: Established in 1983 as the Asian Cricket Conference to foster and develop cricket across the continent.
Headquartered in Colombo, Sri Lanka.
Organizes the biennial Asian Cup tournament for both Men's and Women's national cricket teams.

vocab_words.meaning: To make something bad or unsatisfactory better; to improve.
vocab_words.example_sentence: Digital assessments at RSETIs are designed to ameliorate operational delays in credit disbursement for rural entrepreneurs.

vocab_words.meaning: Equivalent in seriousness, value, or effect to something.
vocab_words.example_sentence: Disregarding regional environmental concerns during ESA notifications is tantamount to ignoring sustainable development principles.

vocab_words.meaning: Intended or likely to placate, pacify, or overcome animosity.
vocab_words.example_sentence: The foreign minister adopted a conciliatory tone to facilitate diplomatic dialogue between the neighboring nations.

vocab_words.meaning: A situation in which no progress is possible; a deadlock or stalemate.
vocab_words.example_sentence: Bilateral trade negotiations reached an impasse over disagreement regarding tariff reductions on agricultural imports.
The chief analyst had the temerity to challenge the central bank's inflation projections during the monetary policy presser.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: To remove tension, doubts, or misunderstandings between people by discussing them openly.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: The bilateral meeting between the two heads of state helped clear the air regarding recent maritime border disputes.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: To issue a challenge or provocation to someone.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: The central government threw down the gauntlet to states by linking infrastructure grants to fiscal reform milestones.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: In strong disagreement or dispute with someone.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: The union and management remain at loggerheads over the proposed revision of pension benefits.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: To prevent something harmful or undesirable from approaching or affecting one.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: Prudent monetary intervention by the central bank helped keep runaway retail inflation at bay.

idioms_of_the_day.idiom: Hit the nail on the head
idioms_of_the_day.meaning: To describe precisely what is causing a situation or problem.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: The Governor's speech hit the nail on the head regarding structural weaknesses in supply chain logistics.

static_gk_boosters.title: Kasturirangan Committee on Western Ghats
bullets: Constituted in 2012 as a High-Level Working Group (HLWG) to review the earlier Madhav Gadgil Commission report on the Western Ghats.
Recommended designating approximately 37% (around 60,000 sq km) of the Western Ghats as Ecologically Sensitive Area (ESA).
Categorized activities into prohibited (mining, thermal power plants, heavy construction) and regulated categories across six states.

static_gk_boosters.title: Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs)
bullets: Institutional framework established jointly by the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), State Governments, and Lead Banks.
Aims to provide short-term skill development training and facilitate credit linkage for rural youth to establish micro-enterprises.
Operates under the umbrella of Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM).

static_gk_boosters.title: Chabahar Port & Strategic Significance
bullets: Located in southeastern Iran in the Gulf of Oman; comprises two main ports: Shahid Kalantari and Shahid Beheshti.
India signed a long-term main contract with Iran's Ports and Maritime Organisation (PMO) through India Ports Global Limited (IPGL).
Serves as the key oceanic port facilitating direct trade bypass around Pakistan into Afghanistan and Central Asia.

static_gk_boosters.title: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
bullets: Established in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference; headquartered in Washington, D.C., USA.
Primary objective is ensuring global monetary stability, facilitating international trade, and providing financial assistance via SDR quotas.
Publishes flagship reports including the World Economic Outlook (WEO) and Global Financial Stability Report (GFSR).

static_gk_boosters.title: Freedom of Peaceful Assembly (Article 19(1)(b))
bullets: Guarantees all citizens the fundamental right to assemble peaceably and without arms under Part III of the Constitution.
Subject to reasonable restrictions under Article 19(3) on grounds of the sovereignty and integrity of India, or public order.
State authorities enforce regulatory measures (e.g., Section 144 of CrPC / Section 163 of BNSS) to regulate designated protest sites.
